name: Anisotropic Noise
definition: A noise function introduced by Goldberg et al. [GZD08] in 2008 that supports high-quality anisotropic filtering by tiling the frequency domain into oriented subbands.
summary: Anisotropic noise is a procedural function that adapts frequency content to non-uniform perspective distortions by blending pre-computed oriented subbands, unlike isotropic noise which forces a trade-off between aliasing and detail loss.
